topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and introduces the lecture's scope and historical context within immunology.

topics.label: Core Principles and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the converging biochemical pathways that initiate complement activation and generate surface-bound convertases.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and promotes inflammation.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins host cells deploy to restrain spontaneous complement activation and protect self-tissue.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes that arise from deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Microbial Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular mechanisms pathogens use to subvert complement defenses, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus and its biotechnological applications.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
